title: Function Caller Ergonomics: Declarative Schema Guards and Backoff-safe Stream Resumers
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Create first-class SDK helpers for function/tool calling that provide declarative schema guards, safe runtime coercion, and ergonomic invocation middleware across Python/TypeScript/Go. This ticket covers: (1) a lightweight schema guard API that can be used at call sites, (2) runtime coercion strategies for common type mismatches (ints/strings/booleans/lists/maps), (3) retry/backoff semantics for function-call failures (including transparent idempotency support), and (4) streaming resumption helpers that make partial outputs resumable and retry-safe without leaking duplicate side-effects.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (py/ts/go) expose a consistent `function_guard(schema)` helper that validates runtime payloads before invoking the runtime and returns normalized data or a well-typed error
A documented set of coercion rules exists and is implemented behind a feature flag: coercion-off (strict) / coercion-on (lenient).
Invocation middleware supports automatic idempotency token attachment and safe retries for non-side-effecting functions; documented opt-out mechanism for user-managed effects.
Streaming client can attach a resume token and replay from last-acked chunk; server semantics clarified so resumed requests do not double-apply side effects by default
End-to-end tests for representative function schemas (nested objects, arrays, enums) pass in py/ts/go with both strict and coerced modes
Design doc and examples published in SDK repo README with code samples for py/ts/go and migration guidance
Integration PRs merged: SDK runtime adaptors updated; no high-severity regressions in CI performance benchmarks
tasks: Design: finalize coercion rules and edge-case table (nullable vs missing, empty-string -> null semantics)
Prototype: TypeScript guard + example runtime adapter (lib/sdk/func-guard.ts)
Implement: Python helper using pydantic-lite shim for runtime validation and coercion
Implement: Go helper that emits typed errors and optional coercion pathways
Middleware: idempotency token middleware and retry/backoff config (exponential with jitter)
Streaming: define resume token format and implement client-side buffer checkpointing
Docs: examples for common patterns, migration notes, and toggles for strict vs lenient mode
Tests: unit + integ harness covering schema mismatches, retries, and stream resumes
Rollout: feature-flagged release across SDKs, staged enablement for customers dependent on compatibility testing
notes: Trade-offs discussed: strict validation prevents surprising server-side coercion but increases friction for older clients; decided to opt for lenient-by-default behind explicit 'coercion' flag in next release and flip in a major if telemetry supports

We need to avoid making side-effecting functions implicit retries. Proposal: server returns a 'retry-safe' header for registered functions; SDK will only auto-retry when header present or when user marks call as idempotent

Resume tokens will be signed (HMAC) on server side to prevent tampering; client will store last acked sequence id and token in local checkpoint. This keeps resume deterministic even if multiple shards process the stream.
Consider adding automatic generation of TypeScript types and Python dataclasses from function schemas as a follow-up (tracked in ENG-79010)

Performance note: runtime validation should be cheap; we prefer single-pass validation + coercion. Benchmarked naive pydantic approaches and chose a micro-shim with fast-path for primitive schemas. See linked perf doc.
